author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 우리나라에서는 매우 드물게 기록되는 새로, 자갈이 많고 메마른 트인 땅에 산다. 곤충이나 식물 씨앗을 주로 먹는다. 우리나라를 비롯해 세계 곳곳에서 개체 수가 줄고 있다.

art.subject: Crested Lark (Galerida cristata), adult (sexes alike, plumage similar all year), as seen on dry open ground in Korea: a long, spiky, pointed crest of dark-streaked feathers on the rear crown, visible even when partly lowered; face pale buff with a weak pale supercilium and brownish ear-coverts; upperparts sandy grey-brown with diffuse darker streaks; wings plain grey-brown; breast buff-white with neat fine dark streaks; belly and flanks unstreaked whitish-buff; tail dark brown with cinnamon-buff outer feathers. Bill long and strong, dark grey-horn above and pinkish below; dark eye; legs pale pinkish-brown.
art.pose: standing on gravelly ground with crest raised, side view
art.scene: Korean dry open ground strewn with gravel; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing on gravel: pointed spiky crest raised on the rear crown, sandy grey-brown streaked upperparts, buff breast with fine dark streaks, long strong slightly curved bill, pinkish legs, short tail
adult, head detail in profile: long narrow pointed crest rising from the rear crown, plain buff face, long heavy bill dark above and pinkish below
adult in flight seen from below: broad rounded wings with rusty-buff underwing, short tail with buff outer feathers, no white trailing edge to the wing
art.build: Stocky, short-tailed lark, a little bigger and bulkier than Eurasian Skylark and clearly larger than a sparrow. Rounded body, short neck, upright stance when alert, crouching when walking. The crest is a few long feathers forming a narrow, pointed spike that sticks up and back from the rear crown. Bill noticeably longer and heavier than a skylark's, with a gently curved culmen. Legs medium length, pinkish. Tail short. In flight broad, rounded wings with rusty-buff underwings, no white trailing edge, and buff (not white) outer tail feathers.
avoid: Do not give it white outer tail feathers or a white trailing edge to the wing; those mark Eurasian Skylark (Alauda arvensis).
Do not draw a short, rounded, bushy crest like a skylark's; the crest is a long, narrow, pointed spike.
Do not paint a short fine bill; the bill is long, heavy and slightly curved.
Do not paint bold dark streaks on the belly and flanks; only the breast is streaked.
